description: The Highway Performance Monitoring System is the national highway information system of the United States, with data on the extent, condition, performance, use and operating characteristics of the nation's highways. It holds administrative and extent data for all public roads and a mix of universe and sample data (pavement condition, lanes, traffic volumes, speed, and more) for arterial and collector functional systems, with summary travel and mileage for the lowest classes. It was developed by the Federal Highway Administration in 1978, replacing biennial condition studies run since 1965, and is reported annually by the States. Coverage is national, down to road sections. Through the US DOT open data catalogue the FHWA publishes State geospatial networks for 2011 to 2024, a national geospatial layer of all sections for 2024 (also as GeoPackage), filtered views such as the National Highway System and Interstates, and tabular roadway sections and samples for 2018 to 2024 plus county summaries; access is free. Caveats: many attributes exist only for sampled sections, State reporting practices differ, and some summary series were discontinued. HPMS is the standard road network, traffic and condition base for network flow, capacity planning, hazard exposure and resilience studies of US highways, and links to the National Bridge Inventory catalogued here.
